description: The WDG heuristic gives CBS a lower bound on how much the cost of a node must still rise, so CBS expands fewer nodes. It builds the *weighted dependency graph*: one vertex per agent, and an edge between two agents that are *dependent*, which means that their MDDs (all their cheapest paths, layered by time) have no combination without a conflict. Each edge gets a weight `Δ`: the optimal sum of costs of the pair alone under its constraints, minus their current costs, from a small CBS over the two agents. The bound is a minimum *edge-weighted vertex cover*: the least total rise `∑ x_i` with `x_a + x_b ≥ Δ_ab` for every edge. It is admissible for sum of costs and at least as strong as DG; where an exact answer is too costly, the crate uses a smaller bound, so it stays admissible.

papers.authors: Jiaoyang Li, Ariel Felner, Eli Boyarski, Hang Ma, Sven Koenig
papers.title: Improved Heuristics for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Conflict-Based Search
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Twenty-Eighth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2019)
